newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SEES JUNE INFLATION SLOWING TO 2.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SEES JUNE INFLATION SLOWING TO 2.3 PCT.

text.p: Romanian monthly inflation is expected to slow to 2.3 percent in June, from 4.3 percent in May, a government official said on Monday.
"This is a provisional figure provided by the National Statistics Board (CNS) and it reflects economic reforms taken earlier this year," senior Reform Ministry official Liviu Lefter told Reuters.
Lefter said the 2.3 percent rate was in line with previous inflation forecasts, with monthly rates expected to keep within a range of 3.0 to 2.0 percent in the second half of 1997.

In February, the centrist government of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea launched tough economic reforms, including price and markets liberalisation. The move sent monthly inflation soaring to a record high of 30.7 percent in March, reflecting fuel, energy and food prices rises.
The government passed a tough budget earlier this year aimed at trimming monthly inflation and reducing bulging budget and current account deficits.
The CNS is expected to release final inflation figures for June later this week. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
